column1: # Game profile of Cozy Land (Switch, 1.0.0 = v0, the base game). Plays on the Mac
# Unity 2023.2.20f1 (IL2CPP) with FMOD, SDK 17.5.8; subsdk0 is the movie module, which plays the RedDeer.Games splash (H.264 + AAC inside sharedassets0.resource) and the title's background videos

# The sdk build needs the node area cut (Ace Attorney Investigations Collection's SDK 17.5.3 constructor, at the same offsets: the SDK-wide rule of dm/tools/sdk_patches.py); the splash needed the H.264 decoder to hand pictures out
# as soon as they are next in presentation order (dm/host/hle_movie_avc.c)

# Controller: the left stick moves the cursor, A places, B goes back, Y opens the item list, L / R switch the category, the D-pad zooms (up / down) and changes the plot's shape (left / right): the 3D pad layout, which has a D-pad

# Game name: only a label for profile listings and the Mac window title; the iOS app name is the game name in the base NSP, and the bundle ID comes from the base game title ID (build_ipa.sh / NSP script)
# load order as on Horizon: main, subsdk*, sdk (subsdk0 = NintendoSDK_movie)
# The NPDM declares 16 MB of system resource, so IsVirtualAddressMemoryEnabled is true: nninitStartup (main+0x907af0) hands application pool − used memory to StandardAllocator as
# virtual address memory and never calls SetMemoryHeapSize. With the node area cut, the heap check found the hardware pool's region taking the alias region to +4.26 GB in
# nninitStartup and set a 1 GB pool, as for Monster Train 2 and Ace Attorney Investigations Collection. Measured on the Mac over 7 minutes of building: 2.0 GB mapped, the alias
# region's high-water mark +3.75 GB of 4.375 GB, 2.2–2.6 GB resident and 1.2–1.5 GB of Metal allocations
# ---- Shader split (shader_split.py; Unity Shader objects, read by unityfs.py) ----
# everything is under Data/: the player's serialized files and the StreamingAssets Addressables bundles
